knowledgeAnswers.rationale: A running conveyor is not cleaned or reached into. The cleaning is referred to the authorised isolation.
Isolation before cleaning is carried out by the authorised person under the site procedure, as the plant code describes (section 3.7 and section 4.5).
A missing guard is reported at once. It is not replaced or left by the cleaner. Guards must be replaced before restart (plant code, sections 3.6 and 3.7).
The plant code says a tag should not be used on its own as an isolation device (section 4.5).

practicalCriteria: On a sample machine diagram, the worker marks each moving part, guard, interlock, pinch point and emergency stop, with none missed.
On a simulated running conveyor with a spill on the belt, the worker keeps clear, does not reach in, does not wipe the belt, and refers the cleaning for isolation.
The worker reports a simulated missing guard and a damaged interlock to the assessor acting as supervisor, with machine, location and time recorded, and does not attempt to restart the machine.
passRule: Pass when all three practical criteria are observed and recorded by the assessor in a supervised desk or walk-through exercise, with no stop-work criterion met. No machine is operated, isolated or repaired. A knowledge check result is not a practical pass.
evidenceRequired: Annotated machine diagram showing the parts and guards identified
Machine condition report for the simulated missing guard and interlock
Referral record for the simulated isolation request
stopWorkCriteria: A running machine is cleaned, wiped or reached into
A guard is removed, bypassed or propped open by the cleaner
The cleaner isolates or restarts a machine
completionRule: Practical sign-off by an assessor only. This assessment does not confer any licence, certificate or competence to isolate, operate or repair plant.
